executiveSummary: Analysis of 20 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 identifies multiple concurrent public health threats across Europe and the Americas. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to generate Elevated concern in the Americas with ongoing animal-to-human spillover risk, while Mpox transmission persists in the Americas region as of April 2026. Yellow fever activity in the Americas and Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome represent serious endemic threats requiring heightened vigilance. Concurrent circulation of seasonal influenza, RSV, pertussis resurgence, dengue, and chikungunya signals a complex multi-pathogen respiratory and arboviral burden across both hemispheres.
bottomLine: The Americas face a critical multi-pathogen threat environment in 2025-2026, with H5N1 avian influenza spillover risk, Mpox spread, and surging vaccine-preventable diseases demanding coordinated regional response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing H5N1 activity
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from infected poultry and wild birds across the Americas
Sustained surveillance alerts suggest continued geographic spread in animal reservoirs
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces, ensure PPE stockpiles for agricultural workers, and accelerate H5N1 candidate vaccine preparedness planning

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 23 2026 confirming ongoing Mpox transmission in the Americas
Sustained regional circulation following 2022-2024 multi-country outbreak history
Risk of clade Ib introduction from Africa remains a concern
threats.action: Strengthen case detection and contact tracing, expand vaccination coverage for high-risk populations, and maintain cross-border surveillance coordination

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 13 2026 indicating active yellow fever cases
Sylvatic transmission cycle activity in forested regions of South America
Vaccination coverage gaps in endemic and border areas increase outbreak potential
threats.action: Reinforce vaccination campaigns in endemic zones, alert travelers to ensure pre-travel immunization, and enhance epizoonotic surveillance in non-human primate populations

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 18 2026 reporting dengue activity across the Americas
Historical trend of record-breaking dengue seasons in 2024-2025 elevating baseline risk
Aedes aegypti vector expansion driven by climate and urbanization continues
threats.action: Scale up vector control programs, strengthen hospital surge capacity for severe dengue, and promote community-level prevention in high-burden countries

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained pertussis resurgence
Waning immunity and suboptimal vaccine coverage driving increased case counts
Multi-country alerts suggest regional rather than localized surge
threats.action: Accelerate catch-up vaccination campaigns, prioritize maternal Tdap vaccination, and strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
signals: PAHO alerts in January 2026 and April 2026 flagging simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation
Southern Hemisphere 2026 influenza season start alert issued April 27 2026
Northern Hemisphere 2025-26 season alert from December 2025 indicating elevated respiratory virus burden
threats.action: Promote annual influenza vaccination, protect vulnerable populations from RSV, and prepare healthcare systems for increased respiratory illness burden

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 10 2026 warning of chikungunya activity
Aedes vector competence and range overlap with dengue zones increases co-epidemic risk
Ongoing autochthonous transmission reported in multiple countries
threats.action: Intensify integrated vector management, enhance clinical recognition and reporting, and monitor for neurological complications in vulnerable groups

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 3 2026 indicating measles cases in the Americas
Importation risk from endemic regions and pandemic-era vaccination gaps
Risk of outbreak in under-vaccinated communities and indigenous populations
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination assessments in subnational areas with coverage below 95%, strengthen case-based surveillance, and ensure outbreak response stockpiles are pre-positioned

selectAgentSummary: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is a BSL-3 select agent and potential pandemic pathogen of concern. Two PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026) document ongoing H5N1 activity in the Americas region, representing the most significant select agent signal in this report set. Mpox virus (Monkeypox), a BSL-3 select agent, also remains in active circulation in the Americas as confirmed by PAHO in April 2026. No BSL-4 pathogen detections were explicitly reported in the available surveillance titles, though Yellow Fever virus (BSL-3) activity was flagged by PAHO in March 2026. These three BSL-3 pathogens collectively represent the highest-priority biosafety concerns in this surveillance cycle.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR signals reported in available surveillance titles; however, Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance remains a background concern in resurgent pertussis outbreaks
Empiric antibiotic use for misdiagnosed viral respiratory illnesses during multi-pathogen season may contribute to community-level AMR pressure
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (PAHO February 2026) may indirectly affect patient populations with diabetes who are at higher risk for infections requiring antibiotic treatment
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory burden (influenza, RSV, pertussis) creating healthcare system stress in both Northern and Southern Hemispheres across consecutive seasons
Arboviral co-circulation of dengue and chikungunya in overlapping Aedes vector zones increases diagnostic confusion and dual-infection risk
Sustained Mpox transmission in the Americas beyond the 2022-2024 outbreak peak suggests endemic establishment rather than controlled elimination
H5N1 persistence in the Americas animal reservoir with repeated human exposure events represents growing pandemic preparedness trigger
Vaccine-preventable disease resurgence (measles, pertussis) linked to COVID-19 pandemic-era immunization disruptions continuing to manifest in 2025-2026
Southern Hemisphere influenza season 2026 beginning as Northern Hemisphere season ends, creating continuous global influenza transmission with limited inter-seasonal gap for vaccine updates
